parties:
Cox's Bazar Pourashava, Police Station-Cox's Bazar Sadar, District- Cox's Bazar
Vs.
Bangladesh and Others
full_judgment: 3. The petitioner, Cox's Bazar Pourashava was established in 1869 and since then it has been functioning and declared by law as a body corporate having perpetual succession. The petitioner, with a view to construct a Central Bus Terminal outside the Cox's Bazar Municipal area, took lease of 4 acres of Government khas land for 99 years at a salami of more than Tk.35,00,000/-. Accordingly, lease deed was executed by the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar on behalf of the Government and handed over possession of the said land to the petitioner. The petitioner made a requisite plane for construction of the Central Bus Terminal and got the same constructed by the L.G.E.D under "Secondary Infrastructure Town Development Project". On completion of the project the petitioner took over possession of the said newly constructed Central Bus Terminal upon the said lease-hold land covered under the lease deed marked Annexure-J(i) and since then has been managing all the affairs of that Bus Terminal . After taking lease of the said land petitioner got the jams of that land mutated in it's name and has been paying rent to the Government since then. Thereafter, respondent No.1 under the signature of one Zakia Sultana, Senior Assistant Secretary issued Memo dated 23.7.2002 (Annexure-C(i) to the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar directing the petitioner to hand over the management of the Cox's Bazar Pourashava Central Bus Terminal to the Cox's Bazar Zila Parishad in public interest. The copy of the aforesaid Memo was communicated to the petitioner by the Deputy Commissioner, Cox's Bazar vide Memo dated 28.7.2002 (Annexure-C). The respondent No.1, without the process of law, cannot take away the said Bus Terminal from the petitioner arbitrarily by issuing such a Memo. marked Annexure C(i). Moreso, the direction of the respondent No.1 to hand over the management of the said Bus Terminal to the disposal of the Zila Parishad is against the Government decision and public policy of the Government which will be crystal clear from Annexure-H. As such the impugned Memos.and the tender notice for leasing out the Bus Terminal of Cox's Bazar Pourashava by the Zila Parishad is motivated, illegal and violative of the petitioner's statutory legal right. In the circumstances the petitioner having no other efficacious alternative remedy has become to this court and obtained the present Rule. At the time of issuance of the Rule, pending hearing of the Rule, operation of the notice published in the "Daily Cox's Bazar" dated 31.7.2002 notifying tender for leasing out the Central Bus Terminal of Cox's Bazar Pourashava was stayed.
